report_md:
# HeatOS: Chelsea data center heat reuse

*Generated 2026-10-03 18:13 from the live HeatOS model.*
*Pitch: Data center heat that neighbors can count on, with a price for that certainty.*

> **Data status.** Building inventory, weather, demand, supply and confidence currently come from MOCK providers (teammates' data and models pending); figures are illustrative.
> Every number below is computed by the model; the source of each input is listed in Appendix A. Inputs marked "assumption - verify" are placeholders to be confirmed.

---

## 1. Decision framework: where heat reuse should go first

HeatOS scores both candidate sites on nine weighted criteria (1-5 scale).

| Criterion | Weight | Chelsea | Lansing | Why |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Demand density | 10% | 5 | 2 | dense multi-family and commercial blocks vs dispersed rural users |
| Source temperature | 10% | 3 | 5 | air-cooled 27-32 C vs liquid-cooled 45-65 C |
| Supply continuity | 10% | 3 | 3 | colocation tenants vs crypto-exposed flexible load |
| Cost of heat displaced | 10% | 5 | 4 | Con Ed steam and oil vs propane and oil |
| Infrastructure cost per MWh | 15% | 3 | 3 | street works in Manhattan vs long rural runs |
| Carbon displaced | 10% | 4 | 4 | steam/gas on a 0.25-0.44 t/MWh grid vs propane/oil on a cleaner grid |
| Local air / water / noise | 10% | 5 | 3 | PM2.5 92nd percentile block vs clean rural air |
| Vulnerable people served | 15% | 5 | 2 | public housing towers next door vs no disadvantaged communities |
| Community acceptance leverage | 10% | 3 | 5 | heat as a host-community benefit for a contested data center |
| **Weighted total** | 100% | **4.00** | **3.35** | |

**Robustness.** Across 100,000 random re-weightings (Dirichlet, alpha = weight x 40) with +/-0.75 noise on every score, **Chelsea ranks first in 96.6% of draws**. Recommendation: **Chelsea**.

Within the chosen site, a building connects only if its best option has a positive 20-year value (financial NPV at 6% plus avoided CO2 at $190/t), and only while the data center has firm capacity left. Buildings are added in priority order: NPV x (1 + equity score) x boiler urgency.

## 2. Data analysis

### Datasets and models
| Component | Method | Datasets | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mock building inventory | hand-placed archetypes; heat = floor area x use-type intensity | synthetic | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| Mock weather | seasonal sinusoid + diurnal + AR(1) noise | synthetic (NYC / Ithaca climate normals, approximate) | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| Mock demand model | degree-day (base 18 C) space heat + hot-water daily profile, calibrated to annual totals | mock building inventory, mock weather | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| Mock supply model | capacity x capture fraction x daily load factor (0.75-0.95) + noise | site config | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| Mock confidence engine | 100 futures, uniform jitter, engine simulator | engine simulator outputs | MOCK (teammate model pending) |
| Mock Jev | rule-based playbook choice | - | MOCK (teammate model pending) |


### Building inventory (40 candidates)
| Heating system | Buildings | Annual heat (MWh) |
|---|---:|---:|
| electric | 1 | 887 |
| gas_boiler | 22 | 51,309 |
| oil | 5 | 9,437 |
| steam | 12 | 39,040 |


### Recommendation (5 buildings connected)
| Building | Use | Option | Phase | 20-yr value NPV | Reasons |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Public high school, 10th Ave & W18th | school | loop hp | 1 | $2,730,903 | high equity, boiler urgent |
| Fulton Houses Tower 3 | public housing | loop hp | 1 | $2,519,975 | high equity, boiler urgent |
| Condominium tower, 10th Ave & W15th | residential | loop hp | 2 | $2,102,181 |  |
| Senior housing residence, 10th Ave & W17th | residential | loop hp | 2 | $946,465 | high equity, boiler urgent, carbon value tips npv |
| Community health clinic, 9th Ave & W17th | clinic | loop hp | 3 | $518,337 | high equity, boiler urgent, carbon value tips npv |


Not connected: 22 buildings with no option of positive value; 13 worthwhile buildings waiting on capacity. Firm capacity used: 2,966 of 3,071 kW.

### Key modelling assumptions
- Heat pump COP = eta x T_hot / (T_hot - T_cold), eta 0.6 (range 0.5-0.8).
- Energy balance closes every simulated hour within 0.1%; a full year simulates in under a second.
- Autopilot: rules (data center heat, then storage, then existing boilers) or MPC (48 h linear program minimizing electricity + fuel + carbon).
- Full parameter list with sources: Appendix A.

## 3. Sustainability impact (full simulated year)

| Metric | Central | Range |
|---|---:|---|
| Heat delivered | 13,173 MWh | |
| Fuel displaced | 15,828 MWh | gas_boiler: 6464.3, oil: 9364.1 |
| Net CO2 avoided | 3,467 t/yr | 3,455-3,479 (grid factor range) |
| Per MW thermal-year | 693 t | sanity band at this utilization 541-705: pass |
| Energy Reuse Factor (ERF) | 0.2967 | reused / IT energy |
| Energy Reuse Effectiveness (ERE) | 1.1033 | (facility - reused) / IT energy |
| Cooling-tower water avoided | 30,897 m3 | evaporation 20,701 m3 |
| Water added via electricity | 20,640 m3 | 2 gal/kWh |
| **Net water** | **10,257 m3** | saved |


### HDR regenerative scorecard (-2 degenerative ... +2 regenerative)
| Category | Baseline | With HeatOS | Baseline basis | Change basis |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Community | -1 | 1 | poverty 83rd percentile, social vulnerability 79th (HDR site packet) | 22% of network heat to public housing; 2 guaranteed buildings |
| Human Health | -2 | 0 | PM2.5 92nd pct, ozone 83rd pct; days over 90 F rising 19 -> 69 by 2050 (HDR site packet) | 100% of connected buildings' heat no longer burned on site |
| Air | -2 | 0 | block-west PM2.5 92nd percentile, ozone 83rd (HDR site packet) | 100% of connected buildings' heat no longer burned on site |
| Carbon | -1 | 2 | fossil boilers and district steam; grid 0.25-0.442 t/MWh | net CO2 avoided = 99% of connected buildings' existing heating emissions (incl. avoided data center cooling) |
| Water | -1 | 0 | cooling-tower evaporation; 500-year floodplain one block away (HDR site packet) | 10,257 m3 of cooling-tower water saved (net) |
| Nutrients | 0 | 0 | no nutrient loading pathway identified | no material change modelled |
| Biodiversity | -1 | -1 | dense urban fabric; noise 56 dB vs 43.9 dB baseline (HDR site packet) | no material change modelled |


## 4. Risk assessment

| Risk | Type | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner | Linked stress test | Modelled result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cold snap beyond design (1-in-50-year) | Climate / technical | Medium | High | Hot-water tanks + borehole storage; every building keeps its boiler or steam; guarantee premiums priced on CVaR95 | Con Ed | polar vortex | backup +10 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 118 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| Anchor tenant leaves 111 8th Ave | Commercial | Medium | High | Phase-gated build-out; heat removal fee indexed to recovered heat; storage buffers the step change | Google / Con Ed | tenant leaves | backup +0 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 26 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| Data center outage | Technical | Low | Medium | Storage ride-through, then boilers; no customer loses heat | Google | server outage | backup -0 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 16 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| More frequent heat waves (19 -> 69 days over 90 F by 2050) | Climate | High | Medium | Two-way loop absorbs office cooling load and sells it | Con Ed | heat wave | backup +0 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 0 MWh; cooling sold 45 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| Electricity price spike | Market | Medium | Medium | MPC autopilot moves buildings to boilers when heat pumps cost more; all-in heat price shields buildings | Con Ed | price spike | backup +0 MWh/week vs normal; storage used 0 MWh; guaranteed missed hours 0 |
| Data center cooling compromised by the network | Technical | Very low | Very high | Hard constraint: the network only takes heat the data center offers; its own cooling stays sized for 100% | Google | - | - |
| UTEN rate case / Local Law 97 changes | Regulatory | Medium | High | Deal clears without LL97 fines in the sensitivity runs before final investment decision (verify) | Con Ed / NYC | - | - |
| Street works and permitting delay | Delivery | High | Medium | Phase by block, starting with the public housing pilot next to the data center | Con Ed / NYC DOT | - | - |
| Building data quality | Data | High (today) | Medium | Replace mock inventory with LL84 + PLUTO + footprints (teammate pipeline in progress) | Data / ML team | - | - |


**Confidence.** Over the next 48 h, P(all connected buildings fully served by the network) = 100%; expected hours on backup 0.0; top uncertainty drivers: Heat pump efficiency 41%, Building heat demand 30%, Electricity price 29% (40 futures, mock_uniform_jitter).

## 5. Implementation vision

### Phase 1: Pilot with public housing and guaranteed buildings
Connect the highest-priority buildings closest to 111 8th Ave: public housing and buildings buying heat guarantees first, with Con Ed building the first loop segment, the data center heat exchanger, and hot-water tanks.
Buildings: Fulton Houses Tower 3, Public high school, 10th Ave & W18th.

### Phase 2: Loop and storage expansion
Extend the ambient loop along the street grid and drill the borehole field so summer heat (including cooling rejected by offices) is stored for winter.
Buildings: Senior housing residence, 10th Ave & W17th, Condominium tower, 10th Ave & W15th.

### Phase 3: Neighborhood infrastructure
Fold the loop into Con Ed's regulated thermal utility (UTEN Act), connecting further buildings as their boilers come up for replacement.
Buildings: Community health clinic, 9th Ave & W17th.

### Who pays, and does everyone come out ahead?
| Party | Upfront | Financed | Annual operating | 20-yr NPV | Payback | P(ahead) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Google (data center) | $0 | $0 | $175,442 | $2,012,304 | 0 | 100% |
| Con Edison (UTEN Act) | $4,505,000 | $0 | $706,275 | $2,160,521 | 7 | 100% |
| Commercial buildings | $0 | $5,632,786 | $625,940 | $1,546,692 | 0 | 100% |
| Public housing (NYCHA) | $0 | $0 | $261,261 | $2,996,637 | 0 | 100% |
| Guarantee buyers (clinic, senior housing) | $0 | $1,259,555 | $108,402 | $-16,195 | not within horizon | 75% |


**Everyone wins?** Not yet. After trying 54 combinations of heat-price discount, grant share and phase timing, guarantee_buyers remain below 80% probability of coming out ahead (guarantee_buyers near break-even). Best terms found: heat price set to 75% of current cost for offtakers (was commercial 85%, guarantee_buyers 85%, public_housing 90%). Further levers: grant support for building-side equipment, lower-cost transfer stations, or a higher heat-removal fee.

## Appendix B: how each headline number is computed
- **Site scores**: engine/site_scoring.py: weights and scores in CRITERIA; robustness = 100,000 Dirichlet draws
- **Recommendation**: engine/recommend.py: per-option 20-yr NPV at the site discount rate + avoided CO2 x carbon price
- **Heat, backup, electricity**: engine/physics.py + engine/sim.py: hourly simulation with energy balance checked every hour
- **Net CO2**: engine/impact.py: fuel displaced x fuel factor - (heat pump + pump electricity) x grid + chiller electricity avoided x grid
- **Water**: engine/impact.py: evaporation = heat (MJ) / 2.26; tower water = evaporation / 0.67; minus 2 gal per kWh of added electricity
- **Party economics**: engine/ledger.py: hourly money flows, capex by party (pipe = minimum spanning tree), NPV at each party's rate
- **Everyone wins / guarantee premiums**: engine/guarantees.py: sampled futures through the simulator; premium = E[refunds] + CVaR95 margin
- **Stress-test results**: engine/scenarios.py: 7-day runs from 12 Jan (heat wave: 10 Jul), stress fired at hour 24, rules autopilot
